questions.question: During which centuries did several Buddhist pilgrims and scholars travel to China on the historic 'silk route'?

options.text: First, second and third centuries AD

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**First, second and third centuries AD**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Several Buddhist pilgrims and scholars, such as **Faxian**, travelled to China during the first, second, and third centuries AD.
 
• These journeys were primarily taken to collect Buddhist scriptures and spread Buddhism in China.
 
• Notable figures like **Faxian** and **Kashyapa Matanga** played crucial roles in the cultural exchanges between India and China during this period.
 
• The Silk Route was a vital conduit for not only trade but also for cultural and religious exchanges.
 
• These travels significantly influenced the development of Buddhism in China.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Faxian**:

 
 
• Faxian was a Chinese Buddhist monk who travelled to India between 399 and 412 AD to collect Buddhist texts.
 
• His journey is documented in his travelogue, "A Record of Buddhist Kingdoms."
 
 
 
• **Silk Route**:
 
 
• The Silk Route was an ancient network of trade routes that connected the East and West.
 
• It was central to cultural interaction through regions of the Asian continent connecting the East and West from China to the Mediterranean Sea.
 
 
 
• **Buddhism in China**:
 
 
• Buddhism was introduced to China during the Han dynasty (206 BC–220 AD).
 
• It became one of the major religions in China, influencing Chinese culture, philosophy, and art.
 
 
 
• **Kashyapa Matanga**:
 
 
• Kashyapa Matanga was an Indian Buddhist monk who is traditionally thought to have first arrived in China in the 1st century AD.
 
• He is credited with helping to establish Buddhism in China.

questions.question: Which of the following is the residential place of Buddhist priests?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vihara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Vihara** is the term used for monasteries or residential places where Buddhist monks and priests reside.
 
• These structures were primarily built near forests or secluded areas to ensure a tranquil environment for meditation and study.
 
• Viharas were initially used as temporary shelters during the rainy season but evolved into permanent monasteries over time.
 
• Architecturally, viharas often included a central courtyard surrounded by residential cells for monks and communal spaces for prayer and learning.
 
• They played a significant role in spreading Buddhist teachings and served as centers of education and community activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stupa:** A dome-shaped structure that serves as a Buddhist shrine, primarily used for meditation and housing relics of Buddha or other revered figures.
 
• **Stambha:** Pillars or columns often inscribed with edicts and teachings of Emperor Ashoka, symbolizing the spread of Buddhism.
 
• **Chaitya:** A prayer hall or assembly hall with a stupa at its center, used for congregational worship and meditation.
 
• **Buddhist Monastic Life:** Monks followed strict disciplinary codes (Vinaya), and Viharas provided an environment for spiritual growth, study, and communal living.
 
• **Spread of Buddhism:** Monasteries like Viharas became centers of learning and played a pivotal role in the dissemination of Buddhist philosophy across Asia.

questions.question: Bharhut Stupa depict the Jataka tales and stories. It is located in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Madhya Pradesh__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**Bharhut Stupa 

 
• Bharhut is well-known for the Buddhist stupa (shrine) ruins that Major General Alexander Cunningham found there in 1873.
 
• The Indian Museum in Kolkata and the Municipal Museum in Allahabad currently house the majority of the stupa's sculpture remnants.
 
• The stupa was likely started during the reign of Ashoka (c. 250 bce).
 
• The Mauryan king Ashoka may have constructed the Bharhut stupa for the first time in the third century BCE, but many decorative elements—particularly the doorway and railings—appear to have been added during the Shunga period, with many reliefs dating to the second century BCE or later.

​Madhya Pradesh

 
• Geographically, this location is located at 23° 31' 0" North and 80° 57' 0" East in Shahdol, Madhya Pradesh, India.
 
• Its original name is Bharhut.
 
• From roughly 268 to 232 BCE, Ashoka the Great, an Indian ruler of the Maurya Empire and the son of Bindusara, governed nearly the entire Indian subcontinent.
 
• In ancient Asia, Ashoka encouraged the spread of Buddhism.
 
• With more than 72 million inhabitants, Madhya Pradesh is the fifth most populous and second-largest state in India by area. Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Rajasthan are its neighbours to the northeast, east, south, west, and northwest, respectively.

questions.question: Which of the following structure is associated with Buddhism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stupa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stupa** is a Buddhist structure that is used for meditation and religious offerings.
 
• It is a dome-shaped structure that represents the Buddha's final resting place and symbolizes the path to enlightenment.
 
• Stupas are found in various parts of the Buddhist world, including **India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Myanmar, and Cambodia**.
 
• They are considered to be one of the most important forms of Buddhist architecture and are often surrounded by smaller shrines and temples.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Pallava is a style of temple architecture that originated in South India during the 7th century CE. It is characterized by its intricate carvings and sculptures.
 
• Mandapa is a pillared hall that is often found in Hindu and Jain temples. It is used for various religious ceremonies and rituals.
 
• Shikhara is a type of tower that is found on top of Hindu and Jain temples. It is often decorated with intricate carvings and sculptures.

questions.question: Dhamma is the ________ word for the Sanskrit word 'Dharma'.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dhamma** is the Pali term for the Sanskrit word **Dharma**.
 
• Pali is an ancient language of the Indian subcontinent, primarily used in the scriptures of Theravada Buddhism.
 
• The **Tipitaka**, the sacred canon of Theravada Buddhism, is composed in Pali.
 
• Dhamma in Pali and Dharma in Sanskrit generally mean the teachings of the Buddha or the universal law.
 
• Pali language played a crucial role in the spread of Buddhism across South and Southeast Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pali Canon:**

 
 
• Also known as the Tipitaka, it is the canonical literature of Theravada Buddhism.
 
• The Tipitaka consists of three "baskets" (pitakas): the Vinaya Pitaka (monastic rules), the Sutta Pitaka (discourses), and the Abhidhamma Pitaka (philosophical and doctrinal analyses).
 
 
 
• **Dharma:**
 
 
• A key concept in Indian religions including Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, and Sikhism.
 
• In Buddhism, it refers to the teachings of the Buddha which lead to enlightenment.
 
 
 
• **Prakrit Languages:**
 
 
• A group of Middle Indo-Aryan languages, among which Pali is one.
 
• Prakrit languages were commonly spoken in ancient India and used in various Jain and Buddhist texts.
 
 
 
• **Tamil:**
 
 
• A Dravidian language spoken predominantly by the Tamil people of India and Sri Lanka.
 
• It is one of the oldest languages in the world with a rich literary tradition.
 
 
 
• **Abahatta:**
 
 
• A later form of Prakrit that evolved into the modern Indo-Aryan languages like Bengali, Assamese, and Oriya.
 
• It was spoken in eastern India during the medieval period.

questions.question: Gautama Buddha attained enlightenment under a peepal tree at _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bodh Gaya. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gautama Buddha **attained** enlightenment **under a **peepal tree at Bodh Gaya, **which is located in the Indian state of** Bihar.**
 
• The peepal tree under which Buddha attained enlightenment is also known as the **Bodhi Tree, **which is considered **sacred by Buddhists.**
 
• **Bodh Gaya is home to the Mahabodhi Temple, **which was built by** Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE** to commemorate Buddha's enlightenment
 
• **The Mahabodhi Temple complex **also** includes the Vajrasana,** which is believed to be the spot where Buddha meditated and attained enlightenment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Important events in the life of Gautama Buddha:**

 
• The Buddha, initially known as **Siddhartha Gautama,** was born into a royal family in **Lumbini,** currently located in **Nepal, in the 6th to 4th century BCE.**
 
• At the age of 29, after witnessing the sufferings of life (old age, sickness, death), Gautama renounced his royal life in **search of the path to end human suffering.**
 
• For several years, he embraced the life of an ascetic, practicing extreme austerity. However, he found this didn't lead to enlightenment and instead advocated for what he called** "the Middle Way"**—a life of moderation away from extreme asceticism and hedonism.
 
• After attaining enlightenment, the Buddha delivered his **first sermon in Sarnath**, near **Varanasi in India**, often referred to as **"Setting the Wheel of Dhamma in Motion**". It marked the beginning of his teaching or the dissemination of his understanding of the "truth" about life and existence.
 
• Buddha initiated a community of followers, both **monks (Bhikkus) and nuns (Bhikkunis).** This Buddhist monastic community, known as Sangha, spread the teachings of Buddha after his death.
 
• The Buddha died at the **age of 80, in Kushinagar, India.** His death is also termed as** Parinirvana, **the final Nirvana. After his death, the Buddha's teachings were collected into written form, called **Tripitaka (Three Baskets),** forming the foundation of Buddhist philosophy and practice.

questions.question: At which Buddhist site of India did Gautama Buddha first preach the Dharma?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarnath**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first sermon was delivered to his 5 disciples at Sarnath in a deer park.
 
• The first sermon delivered by Buddha was on deliverance from suffering.
 
• The event of the first sermon is known as "Dharmachakra Pravartana" which means turning the wheel of dharma.
 
• In the first sermon, Buddha gave two elements of the Holy Trinity of Buddhism.
 
 
• Dhamma: Teachings
 
• Sangha: Order of Buddhist monks and nuns
 
 
 
• His five disciples became Arhats.
 
• Buddha obtained Mahaparinirvana at the age of 80 in Kushinagar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• After attaining Enlightenment Buddha discovered four noble truths:

 
 
• The truth of suffering (Dukkha)
 
• The truth of the cause of suffering (Samudaya)
 
• The truth of the end of suffering (Nirodha), and
 
• The truth of the path that leads to the end of suffering (Astangika-Marga).
 
 
 
• Buddha attained Enlightenment at the age of 35 at Gaya under a Peepal tree at Uruvela.
 
• The Peepal tree under which Buddha attained Enlightenment is the famous Bodhi tree.
